newsitem.title: USA: AT&T to unveil business local service - sources.
newsitem.headline: AT&T to unveil business local service - sources.

text.p: AT&T Corp plans to unveil later Monday its plans to offer local telephone services to business customers in a broad-based plan that initially targets its largest customers, an AT&T source said.

The formal announcement, to be made at a news briefing slated to begin at 1330 EST/1830 GMT Monday afternoon, will be national in scope, the company source said. "We are going to have a very wide footprint throughout the country," he said.
Industry sources familiar with the details of the annoucement said AT&T plans to roll out the local service first in states where it has resale agreements in place.
Analysts said they expected AT&T to introduce local service for business customers in California, Texas, Illinois, Michigan and Iowa, or "places where they already have resale deals in place."
"The delimeter here is that they have the resale agreements and billing arrangements in place," said one industry source.
AT&T's move into local service for business customers is an interim step that would be rolled out in a staged fashion to its largest customers first, the industry sources said.
The AT&T move follows that of rival MCI Communications Corp, which has been offering local service to business customers in 25 U.S. cities since the middle of 1996.

The two approaches differ in that AT&T local service plans will take advantage of resale agreements the company is negotiating with local facilities providers around the nation. MCI's local strategy uses its own network facilities.
